# Axona Protocol — llms.txt
# Serverless peer-to-peer pub/sub. Kernel 4.38.0 / wire 4.0.
# Repo: https://github.com/axona-net/axona-docs

Axona is a peer-to-peer communication substrate: topics are addresses
derived from descriptors, messages route to an emergent per-topic root and
fan out through a distribution tree. No central server, broker, or database.
Authorship is an Ed25519 signature, not an account.

## AI-facing documentation (start here)

- Tier 1 — AI Grounding (hard rules + canonical patterns; keep in context):
  programmer-guide/Axona-AI-Grounding-v4.48.0.md
- Tier 2 — AI Reference (complete API surface: signatures, options, errors,
  timing/behavioral model; sectioned for selective loading):
  programmer-guide/Axona-AI-Reference-v4.48.0.md
- Full corpus in one file: llms-full.txt (also llms-full.md)

## The two rules that prevent 90% of generated-code failures

1. A topic is a descriptor object { region?, owner?, name, write? }, never a
   string; publisher and subscriber must use IDENTICAL fields (mismatch =
   silent no-delivery).
2. Every content operation takes the descriptor FIRST and names its signer:
   pub(topic, msg, {signWith}) · kill(topic, msgId, {signWith}). There is no
   id-only form and no default signer.

## Networks

- testnet:    wss://testnet.axona.net       (newest kernel)
- production: wss://bridge.axona.net (east) + wss://bridge-west.axona.net
- GET /healthz on any bridge → { status, version, kernelVersion }
- Install: npm install github:axona-net/axona-protocol#v4.38.0
